transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-10
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Avery Lang (Redwood AE), Jordan Kim (Redwood SE), Tessa Nguyen (Redwood CSM), Priya Rao (Helios Procurement), Markus Li (Helios Security), Samantha Ortiz (Helios Cloud Architect), Dante Ruiz (Helios FinOps)

Summary:
Quick intake to align on procurement checklist, key MSA/DPA ask-list, SLA targets and technical onboarding constraints (VPC, KMS, SSO). Agreement to run a 4-week pilot (sandbox) and circulate legal redlines + security pack.

Topics: MSA redlines, DPA data flow, KMS/HSM expectations, SLA uptime and credits, pricing approval path, PO/billing cadence, pilot scope and success criteria.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna run through the onboarding playbook and call out the MSA/DPA bits that usually come up. Uh, Priya, thanks for coordinating from your side.
[00:18] Priya (Helios Procurement): Yeah thanks, Avery. Quick ask up front — Helios requires a 60 day review for any MSA redline, and our legal team will want a tracked changes version. Also we need to know SLAs, credits, and data residency implications up front.
[00:32] Avery: Totally. Jordan, wanna run SLA high level?
[00:35] Jordan (Redwood SE): Sure, uh, our hosted API standard is a 99.9% uptime SLA for production, with standard service credits tiered in the MSA. For Dedicated we have 99.95 and for Private on-prem we can do custom SLOs. There was a — sorry — an earlier note that customers sometimes want a 24/7 incident response window; we can accommodate via premium support add-on.
[01:05] Markus (Helios Security): When you say 'service credits', can you clarify the credit metric? Is it token-based, or revenue-based? We need clear measurables in the contract.
[01:17] Jordan: Good question. Credits are fault-time based against monthly uptime percentage, not token usage. So if monthly availability falls below the threshold, credits are applied to the invoice. We can include a sample calculation in the SLA exhibit.
[01:33] Samantha (Helios Cloud): Also need to confirm encryption in transit and at rest. Specifically, can we bring our own KMS? Our compliance requires CMK in our cloud KMS — so KMS/HSM support is a blocker for Private and dedicated.
[01:48] Avery: We support customer-managed keys for Private and Dedicated via KMS integration; for Hosted we offer envelope encryption and an option for tenant-specific CMKs on certain plans. Jordan, any implementation notes?
[01:57] Jordan: Yeah implementation is straightforward — we integrate with AWS KMS or GCP KMS; for HSM-backed keys we support your HSM via external key managers, but that usually needs the private deployment path. I'll attach our KMS integration guide.
[02:12] Priya: Good. On the DPA: data retention periods, deletion guarantees, and logs access are critical. We need audit logs for access to PII and a data retention appendix for 90 day and 365 day retention profiles.
[02:25] Tessa (Redwood CSM): We have a standard DPA with configurable retention settings. For the pilot we can set a shorter retention window and provide access logs; for production we can map controls to Helios' policy.
[02:38] Priya: Perfect. On billing — our finance prefers quarterly invoicing and PO-first procurement for pilots > $10k. Dante, is that within scope?
[02:47] Dante (Helios FinOps): We'll need an approved PO and a three-way match for invoices. Also need clarity on overage thresholds and how they are invoiced.
[02:56] Avery: We'll hand off billing pathways — Tessa will include the pricing sheet and overage rules. Typically we do per-token billing for hosted, but for Dedicated we can do committed monthly retainer with overage rates.
[03:10] Markus: From security, we need SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, and ISO27001 evidence. Also an explanation of network isolation for the Dedicated offering.
[03:21] Jordan: We'll attach SOC2 and ISO artifacts. Network isolation for Dedicated is via tenant VLANs and strict security groups; for Private we do VPC peering and customer-managed routing. Note: sometimes the transcript generator writes K-V cash as K-V 'cash' — that's okay.
[03:37] Priya: Haha noted. Another legal ask: liability cap language — do you generally accept a higher cap for regulated customers?
[03:44] Avery: Our starting point is industry-standard liability cap tied to fees paid in the prior 12 months. For regulated customers we can entertain higher caps but that typically requires an enterprise agreement and underwriting.
[03:55] Priya: Understood. For pilot success criteria Helios wants: latency under 200ms p95 for common flows, classification accuracy not to regress more than 2% versus baseline, and no data leakage in logs.
[04:10] Jordan: Latency target is reasonable for dedicated/good region routing. For hosted we might need to recommend a dedicated pool or model variant to hit 200ms p95 at scale. We'll include a suggested runbook for performance tuning and batching configuration.
[04:26] Samantha: Regarding network: we need to schedule VPC peering; our infra team has maintenance windows on Tuesdays 02:00-06:00 UTC.
[04:34] Avery: We'll coordinate. Jordan, include infra contacts and an onboarding checklist with a peering window template.
[04:40] Jordan: Will do.
[04:44] Markus: A couple of redlines from security: 1) no subprocessing without notice; 2) right to audit clause — we want annual audit rights. How do you handle subcontractors?
[04:56] Tessa: We maintain a subprocessors list and give notice for major changes; audit rights can be scoped to SOC2 evidence and on-site audits are usually by exception and subject to NDA and scheduling.
[05:08] Priya: Can you confirm data residency — some PHI-adjacent data can't leave the EU. Can you restrict processing to eu-west-1?
[05:17] Jordan: Yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we broker region-specific endpoints and can pin workloads to a region for an additional configuration. We'll surface the region residency notes in the DPA appendix.
[05:31] Samantha: For the pilot we'd like to test in eu-west-1 and us-east-1 concurrently. Is that doable?
[05:37] Jordan: Absolutely. We can run cross-region pilots; note there are additional costs for cross-region replication for stateful caches. We'll call that out in the pilot pricing.
[05:47] Dante: On pricing approvals — procurement wants a single consolidated quote that our approvers can attach to a PO. Also we need a breakout: pilot cost, expected month-1 cost if promoted, and a map of overage rules.
[05:58] Avery: Tessa will generate a consolidated quote/worksheet that Dante can use.
[06:04] Priya: Legal will want to review the MSA redline. We'll share an internal playbook of our standard redlines but expect a 60 day turnaround. Are there any MSA clauses Redwood won't deviate on?
[06:15] Avery: We try to be flexible on many commercial clauses; we don't typically change IP assignment around model outputs — that's part of our standard language. We also try to maintain a mutual indemnity; specifics we can discuss offline with legal.
[06:27] Priya: Got it. On data deletion — we need guaranteed deletion within 30 days of contract termination and a certificate of deletion. Is that in the DPA?
[06:36] Jordan: We have deletion guarantees in the DPA, and we can issue a certificate of deletion. For cached transient KV data we delineate retention windows; we'll add explicit language.
[06:47] [Pause / crosstalk]
[07:02] Samantha: Quick technical question on embeddings and vector stores — are those stored by default in the service or do we ship them back to customer S3?
[07:10] Jordan: By default embeddings can be stored in our managed vector store; for customers who require, we can persist embeddings to their S3/GCS via connector or offer a Private dedicated deployment where data never leaves customer environment.
[07:23] Priya: That's important. We prefer using our S3 for any persistent vectors.
[07:29] Jordan: Noted. We'll include the connector spec and auth flow in the architecture doc.
[07:36] Dante: On payment terms — Net30 is preferred. Would Redwood accept Net30 for the pilot?
[07:41] Avery: We can accept Net30 with an approved PO for pilots under enterprise terms; otherwise our self-serve hosted default is immediate invoicing.
[07:50] Priya: Great. Next, about SSO — SAML 2.0 is standard for us; do you support SCIM for provisioning?
[07:58] Tessa: Yes we support SAML and SCIM provisioning for user management in the console. For Private we can do IdP federation as well.
[08:05] Priya: Wonderful.
[08:09] Mark (Helios Security): One more on retention: can we get field-level redaction and PII masking at rest?
[08:16] Jordan: We have PII masking features and redaction pipelines; for guaranteed field-level masking we recommend customization in the pipeline or pre-processing on the customer side.
[08:27] Priya: Okay, let's talk timeline. We want a pilot kick-off in two weeks. Is that workable?
[08:33] Avery: Yes, two weeks is feasible. We'll aim to have the MSA redline and security bundle to you within 2 business days, and the tech pilot kickoff in the week of 2026-02-16.
[08:43] Samantha: We'll need an internal marshal for the peering and test accounts — I'll assign that and confirm by Friday.
[08:50] Dante: Also need a price cap sign-off — I can provide the budget threshold by next Wednesday.
[08:56] Priya: Good.
[09:00] [Discussion — details of pilot scope and specific endpoints]
[12:30] Jordan: (longer technical explanation clipped) ... continuous batching, kv cache behavior when using long running dialog, how to clear cache if keys are rotated.
[18:15] Samantha: Clarifying peering: we want non-overlapping CIDRs and route-only peering not full VPN.
[18:28] Jordan: We support route-based peering, and will provide a template; also note NAT behaviour for egress logging needs to be considered.
[23:03] Priya: Legal question — can we add a clause for data subject access requests (DSAR) support? We need a timeline for Redwood to respond to DSARs.
[23:14] Tessa: Standard DSAR handling is 30 days; we can agree e.g., 10 business days for initial acknowledgment and 30 days for fulfillment depending on complexity. We'll add an operational procedure in the DPA.
[29:44] Markus: On-boarding checklist — could you walk through the sequence so our project manager can map dependencies?
[29:52] Avery: Sure — step 1: legal and DPA sign-off; step 2: infra setup (VPC peering/KMS) ; step 3: account provisioning & SSO; step 4: pilot data ingest & smoke tests; step 5: pilot evaluation and go/no-go. We'll send a checklist.
[30:10] Priya: And who owns step 1 for the redline? Is it our legal with input from Redwood?
[30:15] Avery: Correct — you send redlines, we respond. We'll provide a track-changes MSA within 48 hours of receiving your redline.
[30:23] Samantha: A small note — during the pilot we may need data processor subprocessors listed for third party telemetry.
[30:31] Tessa: We'll include subprocessors and telemetry agreements.
[30:36] [Brief silence, typing noises]
[31:00] Dante: One more — export controls / cross-border transfer clause. Need an explicit carve out for EU-only processing.
[31:08] Jordan: We'll ensure DPA has region-only language option and export control adherence.
[31:15] Priya: Okay, I think we have the items. Any blockers?
[31:20] Avery: None from our side; main dependency is legal turnaround and VPC peering windows.
[31:25] Priya: Perfect.
[31:30] [Wrap up discussion about scheduling]
[32:00] Avery: Quick recap — we'll: send MSA redline, attach SOC2/ISO, provide KMS and network docs, share pilot pricing spreadsheet, and schedule pilot kickoff for w/c 2026-02-16.
[32:12] Priya: We'll circulate Helios' standard redlines and procurement PO template by EOD 2026-02-11.
[32:20] Tessa: I'll own the consolidated quote and onboarding checklist.
[32:25] Jordan: I'll send technical artifacts and network templates.
[32:30] Samantha: I'll confirm the peering window and internal PM by Friday.
[32:35] Dante: I'll finalize the budget cap and PO workflow by 2026-02-18.
[32:40] Markus: We'll review security docs once they're in and get back with any follow-ups.
[32:45] Avery: Great. Thanks everyone.
[32:51] [Call ends — small chatter and goodbyes]

Notes: Some transcription artifacts present (acronyms sometimes mis-heard). Attachments to be sent: MSA redline, DPA appendix, SOC2/ISO artifacts, KMS integration guide, pilot pricing spreadsheet, network peering template.
